version: 4.0 (feature/visual-overhaul-tokyo-4.0, d59e6ba): Tokyo in three render pipelines, interleaved per scenario
machine: Apple M5, Chrome, ANGLE Metal, 120 Hz display, DPR 2. ON BATTERY, 18-20%: Chrome capped requestAnimationFrame at ~31 Hz (Energy Saver) in every pipeline
method: __dev.bench(3, { pipelines: ['v4', 'raw', 'v37'] }) on Balanced applied in memory (pixel ratio 1.25, 60 cap, 3 bloom levels; saved settings unchanged). Per scenario, all three pipelines measured in rotated order; a measurement is valid only if the window stayed focused, visible and in play. All 24 were valid. FPS is capped by the browser here, so per-frame CPU and GPU time are the cost measure; 60 FPS is NOT VERIFIED in this session.

pipelines.v4: composer with the 4.0 look (bloom 0.7/0.9/1.0, teal/orange), 4.0 wet model, reflection catchers, street AO
pipelines.raw: no composer: the world straight to the canvas (ACES + sRGB by the renderer), the same 4.0 materials
pipelines.v37: composer with the 3.7 look (bloom 0.85/0.65/0.92, no split-tone), 3.7 wet model, no catchers, no AO

notes: Run-to-run noise is about ±0.3 ms GPU here; differences between v4 and v37 are within it in every scenario.
The composer chain (bloom, grade, output) costs ~0–0.8 ms over raw.
The 'raw' draw counts are lower because no post passes are drawn; the scenario counts also differ with what moves (train, crowd) during each 3 s window.
Under the Energy Saver cap the CPU and GPU may also run at reduced clocks; compare with a plugged-in run before reading absolute values against BENCH-3.x.
